newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crude prices at standoff pre-Easter.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crude prices at standoff pre-Easter.

text.p: The U.S. West Coast crude market was little changed Thursday ahead of Easter and refinery buyers said they were holding out for lower prices.

Local benchmark Alaska North Slope (ANS) was being offered at 90 cents below West Texas Intermediate/Cushing by suppliers, while buyers were holding out for more than $1.00. The last confirmed deal was on March 13 at 91 cents below WTI.

"I don't think anyone will be willing to do it for less than a buck (discount)," said a California crude trader, adding that trading had slowed after April pipeline scheduling was completed earlier this week.
